summary: Weekly POC sync focused on recent regression signal in extraction recall after prompt pruning; discussed guardrail false positives, quantized model artifacts, and routing fallbacks. topics: Guardrail false positives and threshold tuning
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): ok hi everyone thanks for joining, 10:30 on the dot. quick roll call?
[00:06] Hannah (Veritas): Hannah here, Omar, Priya on my side.
[00:09] Maya: great, Arjun from the SE team with me. we got the updated scorecards from your run last night, so we want to walk through the signal diag.
[00:18] Arjun (SE): quick note, transcript may chop names — the extraction recall dip showed up primarily in the clinical extraction prompt bucket, about a 6 percentage point drop.
[00:30] Omar (Veritas): yeah we noticed that. after we pruned the long prompt context to cut latency it seemed fine in staging but in the live sampling we see missing entities.
[00:40] Arjun: right, so two hypotheses: one is the prompt pruning removed disambiguation examples which lowered recall; two is the 4-bit quant variant we tried introduced tokenization drift — we saw some truncated tokens at the tail.
[00:55] Priya: small Q — are we sure the problem isn't the KV cache? we saw some stale prefixes in the trace logs.
[01:02] Arjun: good call, we checked KV hits but there were intermittent cache evictions during peak. that could make the model see a shorter context.
[01:12] Hannah: and the guardrail thing — we had a few false positives where the safety classifier flagged benign customer names as PII, and that bumped the precision down.
[01:22] Maya: ok, so three vectors: prompt pruning, KV eviction under load, and guardrail threshold sensitivity. let's walk the artifacts. Arjun sent link to scorecard (see meeting notes).
[01:34] Arjun: pointing to the sheets — the precision/recall by prompt family: clinical-extract recall 82 -> 76 after change, precision unchanged. hallucination rate ticked up in the quant run by 1.8%. the per-sequence perplexity also drifted slightly.
[01:52] Omar: that perplexity bit — could that be measurement noise?
[01:56] Arjun: some noise, but we correlate with hallucination examples; many of the failing cases share a short tail tokenization pattern.
[02:05] Maya: operational question — for the 4-bit quant experiment we ran it on Redwood Dedicated pool, correct?
[02:10] Arjun: yes, Dedicated with our quant-runtime, but the variant was experimental so kernel selection fell back to a compatibility path which increased variance.
[02:20] Hannah: what about fallback rules, if the quant candidate produces low confidence do we route to hosted full-precision?
[02:25] Arjun: that's the recommended pattern — route by confidence threshold and fall back to the fp16 variant on Redwood Hosted or a larger family. we can show the routing policy in the Console.
[02:37] Priya: can we get the raw beams for the failing prompts? those are the most helpful.
[02:41] Arjun: yes, I'll attach raw beam outputs and token-level probs to the scorecard.
[02:47] Maya: customers often want deterministic rollback steps — let's plan a runbook drill where we flip to fp16 and exercise the fallback under load.
[02:55] Omar: timeline for that?
[02:58] Maya: propose Jan 26th, 11am PT; we'll simulate peak traffic and validate latency SLOs during fallback.
[03:06] Hannah: works for us.
[03:08] Arjun: on guardrails, we recommend a two-part approach: (1) tighten classifier threshold for PII but add token-aware exceptions for the known customer-name patterns, (2) add a short post-filter for high-precision allowlist.
[03:23] Priya: for the allowlist we need per-customer rules, can Redwood handle route-level RBAC and rule sets?
[03:28] Maya: yes, Redwood Console supports route-level policies and RBAC; we'll share a sample rule snippet.
[03:33] Omar: about cost — your Hosted fallbacks will increase per-token cost, can you quantify?
[03:38] Maya: rough estimate: fallback to hosted fp16 increases per-request CPU+token by about 12-20% depending on batch. I'll send a dedicated vs hosted delta sheet.
[03:47] Hannah: success criteria check — we still target precision@5 >= 88 and 95th latency < 400ms, is that right?
[03:54] Maya: that's what we have from last week, Hannah to confirm final by next wednesday.
[03:58] Hannah: confirm.
[04:00] Arjun: one more technical id: we saw a small memory spike causing KV eviction on Dedicated during gc cycles; switching to a slightly larger instance type or adjusting kv-cache TTL reduced evictions in local repro.
[04:12] Omar: changing instance type impact on cost?
[04:15] Arjun: small bump — about 7% on Dedicated monthly commit. we'll model that in the cost sheet.
[04:22] Priya: on the quantization anomalies, did you try per-channel vs per-tensor quant?
[04:27] Arjun: we tried per-channel for weights and a symmetric 4-bit quant for activations; per-channel reduced error but not fully eliminated the truncated-tail cases.
[04:37] Maya: ok concrete plan: Arjun will re-run the eval across full 2k prompt set (including edge cases Priya will export), attach raw beams; Priya will send failing examples; Maya will circulate pricing and next steps; schedule runbook drill Jan 26.
[04:52] Hannah: sounds good. quick question — do you have a security appendix with KMS/HSM notes?
[04:57] Maya: yes we'll share SOC2 snapshots and KMS integration notes via secure link.
[05:02] Omar: any blockers from Redwood to run the A/B?
[05:05] Arjun: none, just need a short window of staging traffic and the config flag enabled for the quant candidate.
[05:12] Hannah: i'll coordinate staging window with Priya.
[05:15] Maya: cool. closing — recap next steps and owners in the chat. thanks everyone.
[05:21] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional name swaps; some technical terms may be slightly mangled (e.g., per-channel vs per-tensor, Redwood Console spelled as 'Console'). Links referenced: scorecard spreadsheet (link dropped in chat), raw-beams export (artifact link), pilot-pricing-delta (doc link).
